title: Capacity smoothing and shock simulations — NA/EU/APAC forecast (2026 Q3)
content:
Executive summary:

This working sheet models month-by-month GPU capacity and utilization across North America (NA), Europe (EU), and APAC for the 2026 Q3 horizon. The objective is to recommend a smoothing policy (warmpool + throttled pre-warm windows) and verify system behavior under three demand scenarios (baseline growth, aggressive adoption, and short heavy shock). This doc contains: assumptions, a compact forecast matrix, warmpool sizing recommendations, automated trigger thresholds, simulated 72-hour spike impact, rollout timeline for regional capacity activations, an implementation gating checklist, and open questions.

Key assumptions (inputs and units):
- Unit = physical GPU node (H100 equivalent). We normalize older SKUs to H100-eq using conversion factors in linked artifact CONFLUENCE-INFRA-2034.
- Baseline monthly request growth: NA 4.5%, EU 3.2%, APAC 7.0%.
- Typical fleet utilization target (steady-state): 55% token/TPS to balance latency SLAs vs cost.
- Warmpool target (idle ready nodes): 6% of provisioned fleet in NA/EU, 10% in APAC (higher APAC due to launch windows and spot/backfill variability).
- Cold spin-up time (to accept traffic): 6–9 minutes for a full node activation; warmcores reduce this to <15s.
- Pre-warm policy lead time: 12 hours recommended for predictable events; immediate pre-warm for sudden traffic spikes when warmpool >= threshold.

Compact forecast table (H100-eq nodes) — projected active provisioned capacity vs expected demand (peak hourly equivalent). All values are number of nodes.

Months: Jun-2026 | Jul-2026 | Aug-2026 | Sep-2026
Regions rows: PlannedProvision | BaselineDemandPeak | AggressiveDemandPeak | ShockPeakSim (72h) | WarmpoolTarget

NA: 420 | 440 | 462 | 480
BaselineDemandPeak: 310 | 324 | 339 | 354
AggressiveDemandPeak: 310 | 346 | 381 | 420
ShockPeakSim: 310 | 620 | 620 | 620
WarmpoolTarget: 25 | 26 | 28 | 29

EU: 240 | 250 | 260 | 271
BaselineDemandPeak: 165 | 170 | 176 | 182
AggressiveDemandPeak: 165 | 185 | 204 | 224
ShockPeakSim: 165 | 330 | 330 | 330

APAC: 180 | 195 | 212 | 230

AggressiveDemandPeak: 120 | 150 | 182 | 216
ShockPeakSim: 120 | 360 | 360 | 360
WarmpoolTarget: 18 | 20 | 22 | 23

Notes on table: PlannedProvision is what procurement/reservations should aim to have available (active + warmpool). Baseline and aggressive demand correspond to 1.0x and ~1.5x adoption curves respectively. ShockPeakSim models a 2–4x transient demand surge lasting 72 hours (e.g., major customer launch or viral PLG event).

Smoothing and autoscaling policy recommendations:
- Maintain warmpool percentages as above. In practical terms, keep warmpool nodes as non-traffic-bearing but fully loaded images, with health-check routing to swap into the active pool in <15s.
- Pre-warm triggers: when rolling 24-hour forecast shows >= 12% growth vs trailing 24-hour average, start staggered pre-warm to reach 50% of warmpool in 2 hours, 100% in 6 hours.
- Throttle ladder: implement 3-tier throttles at 70%, 85%, and 95% effective utilization with progressive request shedding and model downgrade paths (e.g., LLM-16k -> LLM-8k quantized variant).
- Regional buffer allocation: allocate 2% headroom in NA/EU and 5% in APAC for buffer while planet-wide peaks route to dedicated cold fallback pools.

Shock simulation summary (72-hour event):
- Scenario: APAC experiences 3x normal peak for 72 hours starting Aug-15 00:00 UTC. Traffic growth is sudden (10x in 30 mins), sustained for 72 hours, then drops back.
- With warmpool at recommended sizes and pre-warm at 12-hour lead time, automated scaling ramps across 5 waves (10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) over 2.5 hours. The remaining gap must be filled by fast-burst capacity from reserved burst pool and by cross-region routing to NA/EU within latency budget for non-SLA customers.
- Outcome: tail latency increases by 2–4x for 90th pct requests for ~3 hours in APAC; 95% SLOs remain achievable if cross-region fallback is enabled for non-latency-critical routes.

Rollout timeline (high level) — dependency-sensitive windows and owners:
- 2026-03-22: finalize SKU mix decision and submit reservation requests (owner: Rafael Gomez)
- 2026-04-07: infra CI image for warmpool -> bake & test (owner: Sofia Martinez)
- 2026-05-01 to 2026-05-15: region-level canary (NA then EU then APAC) — deploy warmpool management and throttle ladder (owner: Ethan Li)
- 2026-06-01: enlarge APAC warmpool to 10% and validate 15s swap time under load (owner: Maya Patel)
- 2026-07-10: simulation run: 72-hour shock test (synthetic) across regions; collect telemetry (owner: eng-sre)
- 2026-08-01: capacity go-live for plannedProvision targets (owner: infra-ops)

Implementation gating checklist (must be green before mass rollout):
- Warmpool ping/health-checks stable at <15s swap time across 1000 concurrent handoffs.
- Autoscaler can create and attach nodes within configured budget constraints without manual intervention.
- Cost forecasting model updated to include burst-on-demand pricing and monthly reservation amortization (finance sign-off).
- Cross-region routing policy tested for fallbacks and verified with customer SLA mapping.
- Eviction policy for preemptible/spot instances tested for <60s eviction detection and hot-failover to warmpool.

Open risks and mitigation ideas:
- Risk: supplier SKU delays (H100 shipments). Mitigation: temporary mixed-SKU arbitration and adjust kernel selection to support mixed topologies.
- Risk: sudden 10x traffic spikes exceeding cross-region latency budget. Mitigation: enable degraded model path for read-only or background tasks; partner with sales to notify large customers about throttling behavior.
- Risk: warmpool cost drift if adoption stalls. Mitigation: monthly warmpool resizing job tied to trailing-30-day utilization; auto-scale down warmpool floor to 3% during off-season.

Quick action items (owners):
- Rafael: finalize reservation orders and share cost amortization by 2026-03-20.
- Sofia: complete warmpool image bake and test harness by 2026-04-01.
- Ethan: implement 3-tier throttle ladder in staging and provide test scoreboard by 2026-05-01.
- Maya: schedule synthetic 72-hour shock run and confirm telemetry dashboards 2026-06-15.

Appendix — short calculations (examples):
- NA baseline monthly capacity headroom (Jun): plannedProvision 420 - BaselineDemandPeak 310 = 110 spare nodes (~35% buffer).
- APAC warmpool cost estimate (Jul): warmpool nodes 20 * monthly hourly rate (reservation amortized + OPEX) -> see CONFLUENCE-INFRA-2034 pricing table.

Questions for leadership / unresolved items:
- Approve aggressive reservation for APAC (extra 40 H100-eq) to reduce reliance on burst-on-demand?
- Confirm acceptable user-impact windows for cross-region fallback (max added latency budget per SLO).

This is a working sheet: expect iterative updates after the first synthetic shock run. Add comments inline or append new simulation rows for alternative conversion factors or different SKU mixes.
